To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
trypsinogen expression in colon cancer cell lines is related to cell growth and differentiation.

the trypsinogen present in colon cancer cell lines is trypsinogen 1, that it is mainly present in the zymogen form, and that it is expressed at a high level during the first stages of enterocytic differentiation.
the trypsinogen mRNA and protein were expressed by the colon cancer cell line HT-29 and by the enterocyte-like cell line Caco-2, but not by the non-enterocyte-like cell line HT- 29 Glc+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence of trypsinogen in human colon cancer cell lines and with its expression during cell growth, cell differentiation, and the secretion of this proteolytic enzyme.
the presence and expression of trypsinogen in two colon cancer cells, HT-29 GlC+/- and CACO-2, and in a cell line that never differentiates, HT-29 GIC+.
the expression of a pancreatic trypsinogen during the cell growth and differentiation in human colon carcinoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
trypsinogen expression is related to cell differentiation and that the expression of trypsinogen in colon cancer cell lines is related to their ability to differentiate in vitro and to their origin.
trypsinogen expression in the three cell lines studied is not related to cell differentiation but is rather related to the growth state of the cells.
trypsinogen was expressed in all the colon cancer cell lines tested and that trypsin expression was related to the differentiation state of these cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of trypsinogen in HT-29 colon cancer cells is dependent on the differentiation state.
trypsinogen expression in colon cancer cells varies according to their differentiation state, and trypsinogen may be involved in colon cancer development.

trypsinogen expression in colon carcinoma cell lines varies during the course of cell growth and differentiation, and that trypsin may be involved in the process of differentiation of colon cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trypsinogen expression is a characteristic of differentiated HT-29 GlC+/- and CACO-2 cells and that it may play a role in cell differentiation and/or cell-cell interactions.
trypsinogen expression is not a constant feature of the differentiated cells, but is a dynamic process that varies with cell culture conditions.
trypsinogen expression is a good marker of differentiation in colon cancer cells.
